newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds nosedived on Friday afternoon to end sharply lower, as major technical selling wiped out modest opening gains.
"This is a very unexpected sell-off we're having this afternoon," one dealer said.
Another said the heavy selling was based on technicals.
The bond market took some time to digest the U.S. housing starts which rose a higher-than-expected 2.6 percent in April.
Dealers said the sell-off in Dutch bonds was led by bund futures and based on thin volume in Dutch paper.
"It's gone up on short-covering without volume throughout the week, and today once again there's no volume," one dealer said.

Dealers said market players had became more careful as well because of the three-day holiday weekend, after which the Federal Open Market Committee will hold its long-awaited and much-discussed meeting.
Dealers said market players were no longer convinced the FOMC would decide to hike rates, after recent signs seemed to indicate the U.S. economy wasn't booming beyond reason.
"Chances of a hike are fifty-fifty, throw a penny and that'll tell you," one dealer said.
Dealers noted some switching out of German bonds into their Dutch counterparts, especially in the nine and ten-year segment.
Dutch ten-year bonds had felt some pressure during the day from yesterday's 1.25 billion guilder 2012 issue from Italy.
The ten-year spread between German and Dutch paper has significantly narrowed since the beginning of this week, and stood at -5 basis points late on Friday, down from -10 a week earlier.
At the end of Thursday's trade, Dutch ten-year bonds had yielded only four basis points under their German counterparts.

Dutch economists polled by Reuters were split over the size of the ten-year spread in one months' time, with ING Barings expecting Dutch bonds to yield ten basis points under German paper and NIB Securities forecasting a spread of minus three.
